blog.title: Founder Spotlight: Hana Reyes on Building in Climate Hardware

blog.body:
Hana Reyes (Harvard C'14) spent four years inside a utility before deciding the grid's storage problem was a hardware problem nobody wanted to own.

"Everyone wants to build the software layer," she says. "The software layer is fine. The cells are the thing."

Her company now ships iron-air cells to three regional operators, and she is candid that the first eighteen months were spent failing to convince anyone that duration mattered more than density.
